notes: This is a curated citation list. Statements are vendor-documented design properties, not live tests of a particular device or evidence of exploitability.

claims.statement: Apple documents a hardware Boot ROM root of trust that verifies the Apple signature on the iBoot bootloader before execution.
Apple documents that iBoot verifies the iOS or iPadOS kernel before executing it.
Apple documents separate Secure Enclave Boot ROM verification of the sepOS image hash and signature.
Apple documents a Secure Enclave Boot Monitor on A13 or later SoCs which strengthens measurement of the running sepOS boot chain.
Apple documents that cellular baseband firmware undergoes a separate secure boot using software signatures and keys verified by its processor.
Apple documents that Boot ROM sets the Boot Progress Register in DFU mode on A12 or later SoCs; this is part of Secure Enclave data-access restrictions.

claims.scope: iPhone software update system; contextual for A12–A16
claims.statement: Apple describes the software update system as designed to prevent downgrade attacks. This does not prove individual build signing status.

claims.scope: iPhone update/restore authorization; relevant across A12–A16
claims.statement: Apple documents that install authorization checks versions currently signed by Apple and personalizes approval using the device ECID and anti-replay value; a BuildManifest alone does not establish approval.

claims.scope: iOS and iPadOS system volume during supported software updates
claims.statement: Apple documents that iOS and iPadOS bootloaders check the system volume seal against an Apple-signed value before starting the kernel.
